_: THE DEBT LEDGER. Every public Core method or property that nothing in the
game reaches, with the reason it is still here. Two kinds of reason are
acceptable and no third: `WIRE:` — it is a feature that was built and
disconnected, and the entry names the milestone that connects it; and
`BY DESIGN:` — it is genuinely not the game's to call, and the entry says
This is a ledger and not a mute button, which is a distinction this project
has got wrong before: the first guard written after a cancelled CI run
deleted 24 clips would itself have thrown away the corrected set, because it
checked whether a number went down instead of whether the thing worked. So
the rule here is that an entry is DELETED when the API is wired, an API not
listed here fails the build the moment it appears, and a reason shorter than
fifteen characters is not a reason and fails too.
It started at 131 on 2026-07-31, the day the check was written. That number
is the honest size of `built is not running` in this codebase, and it is the
M16 phase 3 and 4 worklist as much as it is a debt.

allow.Acoustics.AsHeardOnTheLine: WIRE: M18 — the render side of the two above; no caller until they have one.
allow.Acoustics.CanMakeOutWords: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — whether a witness heard words or only a noise, which decides what they can retell.
allow.Acoustics.CanPlaceTheVoice: WIRE: M18 — recognising who is on the line is the phone half of the ID ladder.
allow.Acoustics.LineIntelligibility: WIRE: M18 — the phone layer carries calls but never degrades them; PhoneBook.Damped is the same gap.
allow.Acoustics.OutsideBleed: WIRE: M17 audio — a 0..1 MIXER GAIN for ducking the street bed when the player steps through a door, NOT a dB attenuation. Phase 3 tried to use it to quieten a killing in a back room and that is dimensionally wrong; walls are Perception.WallAttenuation and the room is its ambient floor.
allow.Acoustics.OverheardConfidence: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — a witness who hears the killing without seeing it. Pairs with Violence.KillingConfidence.
allow.Attention.Identified: WIRE: M16 phase 2 — the top of the ID ladder, reached in tests and never read by the game.
allow.CharacterCard.Section: BY DESIGN: prompt-text assembly for the LLM harness. SimHarness and ConversationEngine build cards; the Unity layer never formats a prompt itself.
allow.Combat.Breathe: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — stamina recovery between exchanges.
allow.Detail.CostIndex: WIRE: M17 — the budget side of the same system.
allow.Detail.CrowdFraction: WIRE: M17 — set-dressing density has a Game caller for props and none for crowd; the crowd half was built with it and left.
allow.DoorSwing.AtRest: WIRE: M17 — same; the audio cue for a door finishing its swing has no trigger.
allow.DoorSwing.Set: WIRE: M17 — doors animate through DoorSwing.Step; the explicit set is used when a door is opened by something other than the player, which nothing yet is.
allow.Feud.Involves: WIRE: M19 — helper for FeudsOf, dead for the same reason.
allow.Framing.SideOfLine: WIRE: M17 — the 180-degree rule, computed and never consulted.
allow.Framing.SubjectX: WIRE: M17 — cinematic framing composes the authored beats; the thirds-placement helper is used only by the shot tests.
allow.Framing.WouldCrossTheLine: WIRE: M17 — same, and the one that would actually stop a bad cut.
allow.GameTime.HoursUntil: BY DESIGN: superseded by GameTime.MinutesUntil, which every caller uses. Delete rather than wire — kept listed so the deletion is a decision and not a drift.
allow.GossipMill.IsDiscredited: WIRE: M19 — a rumour the street stopped believing; the mill tracks it and nothing reads it.
allow.HarmBook.FeudsOf: WIRE: M19 — feuds are recorded by Harm and drive nothing; they are the cheapest allegiance signal in the game.
allow.HarmBook.Hottest: WIRE: M19 — which feud is worst right now, for the Director to author against.
allow.Informing.RedirectsInquiry: WIRE: M21 law-as-a-tool, and it needs something that does not exist yet. `Inquiry` is DERIVED from HomicideBook's pressure rather than stored, so there is no value to redirect — pointing the detective elsewhere means the book growing a second subject, which is its own change. Weigh is wired and gated as of tonight; this clause is not, and saying so is the point of this ledger.
allow.Intent.Arg: WIRE: M19 — arguments are parsed and the game only ever reads Intent.Verb, so `press a charge against X` has nowhere to put the X.
allow.LightModel.Aces: BY DESIGN: the ACES tonemap runs in the shader, not on the CPU. The C# copy exists so the pixel gates can predict what the shader will produce, and the sim is its caller.
allow.LightModel.AoRangeCheck: WIRE: M17 — contact shadows; the ambient-occlusion model has no consumer in the scene.
allow.LightModel.ConeBrightness: WIRE: M17 — the falloff for a lamp cone.
allow.LightModel.TemperatureFor: WIRE: M17 — lamp colour temperature is computed and the lights are placed with a hardcoded colour.
allow.LightModel.Transmittance: WIRE: M17 — fog and rain attenuation, modelled and not applied.
allow.LightModel.VignetteParam: BY DESIGN: same — the vignette is a shader uniform and this is the gate's model of it.
allow.Menus.EaseOut: WIRE: M17 — the menu transition curve; the panels use PanelFade and never the menu easing it was written for.
allow.Mixing.Admit: WIRE: M17 — same, the admission decision.
allow.Mixing.Budget: WIRE: M17 — the voice-count budget for simultaneous sounds. Nothing enforces it, so a busy market can start every clip it wants.
allow.Mixing.Protected: WIRE: M17 — same, the channels that must never be ducked.
allow.MotionDatabase.ClipOf: WIRE: M17.1 — motion matching queries the database; the whole system is waiting on the Mixamo clips being imported as Humanoid.
allow.MusicModel.RoomHasGoneQuiet: WIRE: M17 — the music layer reacts to tension and not to a room emptying, which is the better cue of the two.
allow.OperationPlan.Bringing: WIRE: M19 — visible odds. The plan knows what you are carrying into a job and the player cannot see it.
allow.Palette.NaiveScale: BY DESIGN: the deliberately-wrong scaling, kept as the contrast case in the palette tests. Wiring it would be a bug.
allow.Palette.Saturation: BY DESIGN: the palette sweep is applied in the post shader; the C# model is what the pixel gates compare against.
allow.PanelFade.SnapOff: WIRE: M17 — instant hide, for a panel closed by a hard cut rather than a fade.
allow.PanelSwap.ToA: WIRE: M17 — crossfade between two panels, built for the pause menu and never mounted.
allow.Payment.InFull: WIRE: M19 — a debt settled completely rather than partially; the purse records it and no UI or reaction reads it.
allow.Perception.HeardAs: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — how a sound is classified by somebody who did not see it. The fight makes sounds and nobody classifies them.
allow.Perception.SymmetryPredictsSeen: BY DESIGN: an invariant the perception tests assert — that seeing is symmetric — rather than a function the game calls.
allow.PhoneBook.Damped: WIRE: M18 — line quality; pairs with Acoustics.LineIntelligibility.
allow.PhoneBook.LinesFor: WIRE: M18 — who can be reached at which number.
allow.PhoneBook.ReachableNow: WIRE: M18 — whether they would pick up at this hour.
allow.PlayerIdentity.InTalk: WIRE: M18 — how the player refers to themselves in conversation, which changes once anybody knows them by name.
allow.Population.InBand: BY DESIGN: the LOD band query used by the population tests and by BalanceLab's distribution checks. The game asks for residents by district, never by band.
allow.PurseBook.Owed: WIRE: M19 — what is owed to you, for the debt-collection loop.
allow.Reaction.Confront: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — an NPC who saw you do it walking over. The single most visible missing reaction in the game.
allow.ResponseValidator.TellCount: BY DESIGN: a measurement the LLM harness reports on generated dialogue. The game validates a response with Validate; the count is for the report.
allow.Rig.FootHeight: WIRE: M17.1 — foot IK, which the roadmap's done-condition for M17.1 names explicitly.
allow.Rig.TwoBone: WIRE: M17.1 — two-bone IK for the arms. Waiting on a real skeleton; the mannequin has no arms to solve.
allow.StreetMap.AvenueClear: WIRE: M17 — whether an avenue is unobstructed, for traffic and for the camera.
allow.StreetMap.FullyConnected: BY DESIGN: a map invariant the tests and the sim assert after generation. The game never re-checks connectivity at runtime.
allow.StreetMap.OnStreet: WIRE: M17 — nearest-street lookup for placing things.
allow.SyntheticCorpus.Query: BY DESIGN: the stand-in corpus the motion tests run against, so MotionMatch can be tested with no clips on disk. Replaced by the real database at M17.1, not called by the game either way.
allow.TrafficSim.AwakeCount: BY DESIGN: an LOD measurement the sim's performance gate reads. The game does not choose how many vehicles are awake; TrafficSim does.
allow.TrafficSim.BusLoop: WIRE: M17 — the bus route exists and no bus is drawn following it.
allow.TrafficSim.NearestTo: WIRE: M17 — nearest vehicle to a point, for the collision and camera work.
allow.Typography.LiftToMeet: WIRE: M17 — the fix-up that makes a failing pair pass.
allow.Typography.LineHeight: WIRE: M17 — the type scale is computed in Core and the UI sets sizes by hand, which is how they drift apart.
allow.Typography.MeasureIsReadable: WIRE: M17 — line-length check for the caption bar and the panels.
allow.Typography.MeetsAa: WIRE: M17 — the accessibility contrast gate, which M22 names and nothing enforces.
allow.Vehicle.Waiting: WIRE: M17 — a stopped vehicle should idle differently from a moving one.
allow.VerbBeat.PhaseProgress: WIRE: M17 — how far through an interaction beat the player is, for the progress ring nothing draws yet.
allow.VerbSpec.WithArg: BY DESIGN: builder used to declare the verb table inside IntentRouter; the game consumes the table, never authors one.
allow.VoiceBank.PoolVoices: WIRE: M17.2 — the crowd voice pool. The named cast is wired; the pool the crowd draws from is not.
